ALG-H5-01.solved: Infinitely many solutions => second equation is a multiple of the first. y-coeff -15 / -5 = 3, so a = 3*3 = 9 and b = 3*12 = 36; a + b = 45.
ALG-H5-01.note: 21 = 9 + 12 (forgot to scale b), 36 = b alone, 39 = 3 + 36 (used the scale factor as a). Textbook module-1 item; one idea only. BATCH-LEVEL: my 24 picks fall exactly 6/6/6/6 across A/B/C/D. An exact-uniform histogram is not evidence of a shuffle - it is the signature of deliberate balancing, and per this project's history (the complete-ABCD-permutation cohort) a perfect histogram has hidden a tell before. I checked consecutive groups of four and found no repeating permutation (1-4 is C,A,B,D but 5-8 is A,C,D,D), so the group-level version of that tell is absent here.

ALG-H5-04.solved: Case x >= 10: x - 10 = 2x - 8 => x = -2, contradicts the case and makes RHS negative, reject. Case x < 10: 10 - x = 2x - 8 => 3x = 18 => x = 6; check |6-10| = 4 = 2(6)-8. So x = 6.
ALG-H5-04.note: -2 is the extraneous root and is a genuinely strong trap; 18 comes from 3x = 18 mis-solved. Case split plus an extraneous check is the closest this batch gets to two interacting ideas, but it is a standard SAT medium, not hard.

ALG-H5-05.note: Routine two-variable mixture; 24 and 21 are near-miss arithmetic, 15 is the 25%-solution answer mis-assigned? not cleanly derivable. Standard.

ALG-H5-06.note: 20 is the strict/non-strict slip, 6 answers the wrong end of the interval, 14 is weak.

ALG-H5-10.note: 24 comes from slope +5/2 with a sign slip on the point, 3 from using slope -2/5. Two steps but they are sequential, not interacting.

ALG-H5-15.solved: 180 + 45d <= 2300 => 45d <= 2120 => d <= 47.1, so at most 47 days; but d must be a whole number of weeks, so d is a multiple of 7 and the greatest such value <= 47 is 42.
ALG-H5-15.note: The one item in the batch where two constraints genuinely interact: the budget cap alone gives 47, and the divisibility condition alone gives no bound - you need both. 47 is the strongest distractor in the whole file; 6 answers in weeks; 49 is the 'round the weeks up' slip. Even so this sits at the lower edge of module-2 hard.
